description: Review Section 3 (spec + quality)

You are reviewing one unit's implementation: first whether it matches its requirements, then whether it is well-built. This is a unit-scoped gate, not a merge review; a broad whole-branch review happens separately after all sections are complete. The unit is Section 3 of OpenSpec change `demo` (task file openspec/changes/demo/tasks.md); its files are src/Ledger.php and tests/LedgerTest.php.

## What Was Requested

Read the section brief first: /repo/.superpowers/sdd/demo/section-3-brief.md

Global constraints that bind this section: the normative lines of the change's spec deltas under /repo/openspec/changes/demo/specs/ that the brief cites. Read only those requirement and scenario lines; they are the binding authority over the brief.

## What the Implementer Claims They Built

Read the implementer's report: /repo/.superpowers/sdd/demo/section-3-report.md

## Diff Under Review

Base: c1d2e3f
Head: d4e5f6a
Diff file: /repo/.superpowers/sdd/demo/review-c1d2e3f..d4e5f6a.diff

Read the diff file once: it contains the commit list, a stat summary, and the full diff with surrounding context, and it is your view of the change. The diff's context lines ARE the changed files: do not Read a changed file separately unless a hunk you must judge is cut off mid-function, and say so in your report. Do not re-run git commands. If the diff file is missing, fetch the diff yourself with `git diff --stat c1d2e3f..d4e5f6a` and `git diff c1d2e3f..d4e5f6a`. Do not crawl the broader codebase. Inspect code outside the diff only to evaluate a concrete risk you can name, one focused check per named risk, and name both the risk and what you checked in your report. Cross-cutting changes are legitimate named risks: if the diff changes a function or API contract or shared mutable state, checking the call sites is the right method.

Your review is read-only on this checkout. Do not mutate the working tree, the index, HEAD, or branch state in any way.

## You Do Not Dispatch Subagents

Do all of this review yourself. Never spawn a subagent to review part of the diff, and never spawn another reviewer for a second opinion. If the diff feels too large for one pass, review it in passes yourself and say so in your report.

## Do Not Trust the Report

Treat the implementer's report as unverified claims about the code. Verify the claims against the diff. Design rationales in the report are claims too; a stated rationale never downgrades a finding's severity.

## Tests

The implementer already ran the tests and reported results for exactly this code. Do not re-run the suite to confirm their report. Run a test only when reading the code raises a specific doubt that no existing run answers, and then a focused test, never a package-wide suite. Warnings or other noise in the reported test output are findings. If the report's test evidence looks truncated or missing, re-read the file at its stated path, and if it is genuinely missing, report that as a gap for the controller.

## Part 1: Spec Compliance

Compare the diff against What Was Requested: Missing (requirements skipped or claimed without implementing), Extra (features not requested, over-engineering), Misunderstood (right feature built the wrong way). Check the diff against the brief's file list file by file: a listed file the diff never touches is a Missing finding. A requirement you cannot verify from this diff alone (it lives in unchanged code or spans sections) is a cannot-verify item, not a reason to broaden your search.

## Part 2: Code Quality

Separation of concerns, error handling, DRY without premature abstraction, edge cases. Tests: do the new and changed tests verify real behavior, not mocks, and are the section's edge cases covered? Structure: one clear responsibility per file, the file structure the brief names, no new oversized files. Point at evidence: file:line for every finding and for every check you would otherwise answer with a bare yes.

## Calibration

Categorize issues by actual severity. Important means this section cannot be trusted until it is fixed: incorrect or fragile behavior, a missed requirement, or maintainability damage you would block a merge over (verbatim duplication of a logic block, swallowed errors, tests that assert nothing). Coverage that could be broader and polish suggestions are Minor. If the brief or spec explicitly mandates something this rubric calls a defect, that IS a finding: report it as Important, labeled plan-mandated.

## Output

Write the full report (Spec Compliance with any cannot-verify items, Strengths, Issues as Critical, Important and Minor with file:line, what is wrong, why it matters and how to fix, then Assessment) to this review file: /repo/.superpowers/sdd/demo/section-3-review.md
